title: The Beginning of the End
logline: One ordinary day in a modern city, dawn to night. The minor signs described fourteen centuries ago sit quietly inside everyday life.

quote.text: They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival? Say, ‘Its knowledge is only with my Lord.’

vo:
The world doesn't end with a bang. It ends slowly… one ordinary morning at a time.
This city wakes before the sun. Kitchen lights flicker on. Engines cough awake. The call to prayer rises over a hundred phone alarms.
By seven, the streets are full. Millions of people. One goal: survive one more day.
The towers keep rising. From the top, the people below are just dots.
The news moves faster now. An earthquake here. A war there. Whole peoples wiped out, while the world watches. A life taken over almost nothing. A man trusted with everything… betrays it all.
Read. Swipe. Forgotten.
And the days feel shorter. Morning starts… and suddenly, it's night again.
Nothing seems wrong. But all of this, towers racing for the sky, trust placed in the wrong hands, the earth shaking again and again, killing that no longer shocks anyone, time slipping away, was foretold by the Prophet Muhammad, fourteen hundred years ago.
When the end will come, no one knows. Only God.
Night falls like any other night. The lights go out, one by one.
Tomorrow morning, a message will spread through the entire city… about something that never happened.
caption:
The world doesn't end with a bang. It ends one ordinary morning at a time.

#endtimes #islam #signsofthehour
sources: Competing in tall buildings: Sahih Muslim 8; Sahih al-Bukhari 50, 7121
Trust neglected, authority given to the unqualified: Sahih al-Bukhari 59
Earthquakes, killing (harj), time passing quickly, two great groups fighting: Sahih al-Bukhari 7121
Only God knows the Hour: Qur’an 7:187, 31:34

classification.canonical: The conditions named in the recap line and the statement that only God knows the time.
classification.interpretation: “A war there. Whole peoples wiped out” read as part of harj (much killing) and fighting in Bukhari 7121; “genocide” is modern language, not a hadith term. The opening line is the series’ storytelling voice, not a claim about timing.
classification.fiction: All people, the city, every headline (generic, no real events, places or organisations), the notifications and the false message at the end.

title: Faster Than the Truth
phase: Phase 01 → 02 · The Age of Fitnah begins
logline: A rumour that the water is poisoned spreads mouth to mouth and nearly ends with a crowd stoning an innocent newcomer. The water was clean all along.

quote.text: Believers, if a troublemaker brings you news, check it first, in case you wrong others unwittingly and later regret what you have done.

vo:
By sunrise, the whole city knew.
The only problem… none of it was true.
It started as one whisper at a food stall.
The water is poisoned.
Someone saw a stranger by the water tower last night.
Nobody asked who saw him.
Nobody asked how they knew.
By seven, the shelves were empty.
Mothers poured water down the drain.
Old men argued at the mosque gate.
And the story grew with every mouth it passed through.
One stranger became three. Poison became a plan.
By noon, they found him.
A young man, new in the neighborhood.
He had been fixing a leaking pipe… for free.
The crowd closed in.
Someone picked up a stone.
Then the mosque speaker crackled.
The water had been tested. It was clean. It always had been.
The crowd went home.
No one said sorry. No one asked who started it.
The warning had been written long ago.
And the Prophet said that repeating everything you hear is lie enough.
That night, a new whisper began. This time, it named someone everyone trusted.
caption:
By sunrise, the whole city knew. None of it was true.

title: The Man From Nowhere
logline: A rumour sets a whole city on fire. The mayor vanishes. On the fifth day a man with no past walks out of the ashes, and on the seventh he tells a full stadium that God sent him.

quote.text: …till about thirty Dajjals (liars) appear, and each one of them will claim that he is Allah’s Messenger.

vo:
The fire started at midnight.
By sunrise, city hall was gone.
Three days earlier, it was only a whisper.
The mayor had sold the city's water.
There was no proof. There didn't need to be.
By the second day, a million people filled the streets.
Banners hung from every bridge.
Half the city wanted him gone.
The other half swore he was innocent.
On the third night, someone threw the first flame.
The mayor vanished.
No one knows if he ran… or if he was taken.
For two days, the city had no one.
No water. No bread. No answers.
Then, on the fifth day, a man walked out of the ashes.
No name. No past.
He handed out bread. He spoke softly.
Everything he said sounded true.
By the seventh day, the stadium was full.
And he told them God had sent him.
Half the city fell to its knees.
The Prophet warned that before the Hour, around thirty liars would come, each claiming to be a messenger of God.
The next morning, the neighboring city heard his name.
caption:
The fire started at midnight. By the seventh day, half the city was on its knees.

classification.interpretation: Presenting a modern false claimant who rises from civil chaos as an example of that warning.

title: The Loudest Voice
logline: His followers take eleven cities with crowds, not weapons. Everywhere, the people who know how things work are pushed aside, and the loudest voices take their place. A new bridge falls, empty, on the third night.

quote.text: When honesty is lost, then wait for the Hour.

vo:
In thirty days, his followers took eleven cities.
They didn't need weapons.
They only needed crowds.
In every city, the same thing happened.
The people who knew how things worked were pushed aside…
and the loudest voices took their place.
A man with no training ran the hospital.
A man who could barely read rewrote the schools.
A new bridge was built by people who had never built anything.
On the day it opened, the crowds cheered.
On the third night, it fell.
No one was on it. Not yet.
The engineers who warned them had already been silenced.
A man once asked the Prophet when the Hour would come. He said: when trust is lost. And when authority is handed to those unfit for it.
Across the country, the experts packed their bags.
The loud ones stayed.
And in the capital, the man from nowhere gave his next order: close the libraries.
caption:
They didn't need weapons. They only needed crowds.

title: Old Gods
logline: The libraries close, the old teachers die with no one to replace them, and on a hill outside the city people begin to walk in circles around an ancient stone figure. Then the money comes.

quote.text: Religious knowledge will be taken away (by the death of Religious learned men).

vo:
The libraries closed on a Monday.
By Friday, no one remembered why they had been open.
The old teachers grew quiet.
One by one, they died.
And no one took their place.
Children learned chants instead of letters.
Parents stopped asking questions they couldn't answer.
And on the hill outside the city, something old was uncovered.
A stone figure, buried for centuries.
At first, people only came to look.
Then they brought flowers.
Then they began to walk around it… slowly… in circles.
No one told them to. It just felt right.
The Prophet said that before the Hour, knowledge would be taken away, ignorance would spread, and some would return to the idols of old.
That spring, the rain came early.
The harvest was the biggest anyone had ever seen.
And with it came more money than anyone knew what to do with.
caption:
The libraries closed on a Monday. By Friday, no one remembered why they had been open.
